messages:
alice_support: Hey team — customer reported rerank calls started failing after yesterday's migration. They see 404 / deprecated model errors and some requests returning identical scores. Attaching example curl and response.

alice_support: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rerank-legacy-v1","queries":["q1"],"candidates":["a","b","c"]}'

Response: 404 {"error":"model_not_found","message":"Model 'rerank-legacy-v1' is deprecated or removed"}

alice_support: Customer says this used to work until last night, they're on a sales tenant (tenant_id=acme-42). Need quick workaround and root cause.

ben_eng: Thanks, pinging infra. Can you share thread_ts from the failing request and a sample request id? Also asking if they use an alias or direct model_id.

alice_support: request_id=rid_0a1b2c, they call model id directly from client-side config (hardcoded). No alias layer in their code.

mike_sre: I pulled logs for tenant acme-42 and request rid_0a1b2c. Backend returned 404 at model-resolver stage. See snippet: 
[INF] 2026-03-05T18:12:02Z resolver: lookup modelId=rerank-legacy-v1 -> not found (deleted)

mike_sre: Also noticed an alias regen event in deployment: alias 'rerank-legacy' was regenerated yesterday as part of model onboarding (INF-1234). Old direct model ids were rotated and some tenants using hardcoded ids lost mapping.

alice_support: So customer used a hardcoded model id that was rotated. Can we redirect or restore? They are blocked in prod.

ben_eng: Short term: ask them to call the stable alias 'rerank-stable-v2' — that alias still points to the compatible reranker model. I'll drop the exact curl to test.

ben_eng: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rerank-stable-v2","queries":["q1"],"candidates":["a","b","c"]}'

ben_eng: If they still see identical scores after switching, send exact body — sometimes clients flatten nested arrays which ends up scoring the same vector for each candidate.

alice_support: I passed the alias suggestion. Customer tried it and got 200 but scores are all 0.5,0.5,0.5 (identical). They attached the request body; I forwarded it.

mike_sre: Identical scores usually mean candidate vectors identical or model returned fallback uniform distribution. Checking model backend: no runtime errors. Looks like the client SDK may be serializing the candidates as a single string. Can you paste the body exactly as it left their client?

alice_support: They pasted: {"model":"rerank-stable-v2","queries":"q1","candidates":"a|b|c"} (yikes)

ben_eng: Yep — that explains uniform scores. Client is sending queries/candidates as delimited strings. Rerank expects queries: ["q1"] and candidates: ["a","b","c"]. Please instruct them to use JSON arrays or the official SDK.

alice_support: Sent instructions and quick fix code snippet to convert to arrays. Also told them to avoid hardcoding model ids and use tenant aliases.

support-bot: Created ticket INF-1234 in infra backlog and linked to tenant acme-42 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1234).

ben_eng: Long term: we'll add a resolver fallback to map common rotated ids to current alias for 7 days and emit a deprecation header so clients can detect. Filed engineering subtask INF-1234-1.

alice_support: Customer confirmed test with arrays: 200 OK, scores look plausible. They rolled the fix to prod.

alice_support: Marking resolved on our side. Leaving notes for onboarding docs to emphasize aliases vs model id. :white_check_mark:

mike_sre: Follow-up action: run a query to find tenants with hardcoded known-rotated ids and reach out. I'll schedule a scan.

ben_eng: Thanks all. Closing thread after postmortem write-up.
